ECHO Studio — Edition 02

Decision and scope

Added /studio/ beside Current / Original. Existing experiences and Character Lab retain their source and assets. Uses the existing self-hosted Three.js r170 and MPFB CC0 base model, cloned with separate skeletons into one scene/renderer. No runtime dependencies, APIs or paid services added. The site audience is unchanged.

Forest, sage and ivory editorial room, slatted wall, architectural practicals, beveled oval table, rounded upholstered chairs and restrained tabletop microphones. Three styling variants share one base mesh. Legs are posed by world-space bone aiming, retaining the actual rig's rest transforms. Hips sit at approximately 0.54m, toes at 0.036m; wrists sit at 0.855m above a 0.825m tabletop. These joint checks are not mesh-level collision proof. Hands remain nearly still; shoulder emphasis is deliberately small. Geometric seated posing is not a commissioned seated animation.

Playback and direction

70.57-second original scripted conversation including pauses, 10 prerecorded turns, 29 audio-aligned caption chunks. One HTMLAudioElement; currentTime drives visemes/captions. Synthetic audio generated offline with Piper; all cast members share the same source voice, openly disclosed. Timings derive from synthesis alignment; they are not measured human lip-sync accuracy. No amplitude-based phoneme claim.

Director accepts turn-start and authored sentence cues. Default minimum hold 5.5 seconds. Actual script has 10 cuts after the opening: speaker mediums, ECHO + Nova two-shot and a chosen Atlas listening reaction. Long holds are intentional across short interjections. All cameras remain on the audience side of the table. Clean cuts, no orbit/tween. Fixed camera is user-controlled. Reduced motion disables breathing/nods/emphasis; cuts are retained without interpolated motion.

Provider boundary

room.js knows no voice or LLM service. MockAdapter in core.js emits semantic events consumed by studio.js:

- turn-start, turn-end: {speaker, text, utterance, time}.

- timing: current audio playback seconds (also accessible through adapter.audio.currentTime).

- utterance: {id, speaker, text, audio, duration, pause, cues?, captions?, shot?, reaction?, reactionAt?}.

- Optional cues: {start,end,key}; key maps to viseme_PP, viseme_aa, etc. Missing cues produce a closed mouth; do not fabricate phonemes.

- Optional expression/gesture extensions should be semantic cues translated into the room performance layer. Current mock consumes one restrained listening nod (reaction, reactionAt) and a small speaking emphasis. It does not implement arbitrary emotion animation or full-body gesture retargeting.

- interruption, cancel, failure, state, reset, mute support transport lifecycle. Interrupt cancels the current playback and resets that turn; Resume restarts it. Pause preserves the playback offset.

A live adapter should serialize audio, supply timing, and cancel buffered/pending turns with a generation token. Streaming buffering, backend authentication, LLM orchestration, network retry and provider-specific viseme translation remain future work. Credentials must stay server-side. Rendering does not need rebuilding for a different provider.

Rendering and mobile budget

One renderer; one 18.5MB GLB fetch, shared geometry with three independent skeletons and cloned materials. Source GLB has 83,686 triangles before hidden eye mesh suppression and added styling/room geometry. DPR capped at 1.25 on narrow screens and 1.5 otherwise, dropping to 1 if measured frame intervals exceed 50ms over 90 samples. No postprocessing or shadow maps. Authored radial contact shading grounds chairs, table and cups. Wall slats use one 49-instance mesh instead of 49 separate meshes. Small cylinders use 16 radial segments. Morph bindings and pose temporaries are cached; the viseme cursor advances once per frame; unchanged caption text is not rewritten. Playback loop targets at most approximately 30 updates/sec; this is a scheduling cap, not achieved FPS. Runtime window.EchoStudio.getState() reports actual renderer counters. Static paused state renders on demand only. Hidden tabs pause audio and cancel the frame request; explicit Resume is required.

Portrait camera compositions, safe-area footer, 44px controls, captions outside the canvas. Audio begins only from a click. Loader, replay, mute, errors, context loss and no-WebGL audio/transcript fallback included. Scene load failure retains recorded playback. Dialogue load failure reports an unavailable state and reload action.

Verification performed

- JavaScript syntax checks for all added modules and shared switcher.

- Real GLTFLoader parsing (textures stripped only in test memory), independent skeletons, 2,817 sampled skinned vertices finite.

- Wrist and toe joint positions, tabletop ellipse membership, face bounds in 25 shot/aspect combinations (320/480, 360/440, 390/440, 768/570, 1240/570).

- Mock transport checks: pause/resume offsets, replay, interruption/restart, mute, failure/retry, cancellation, one pending gap timer, fixed camera.

- Rehearsed full script events: 70.57s, minimum cut holds, authored two-shot and reaction reached.

- All ten MP3 assets decode; metadata within 0.1 seconds, cue duration matches source duration. Caption text reconstructs source utterances.

- Local asset/link existence and unchanged Current/Original application files reviewed.

Commands:

node tests/studio-transport.mjs

node --experimental-loader=./tests/three-loader.mjs tests/studio-rig.mjs

node --check dist/studio/studio.js

Verification limits / follow-up

Managed Sites browser-control skill is unavailable. Per Sites workflow, no preview server or unsupported browser automation was started. No browser visual QA, audible playback inspection, Safari touch test, full mesh/furniture collision test or device FPS/battery benchmark was performed. Geometry checks do not establish flawless skin deformation, palm orientation, eye material appearance or perceptual lip sync. The 18.5MB character asset needs further mesh/texture optimization before broad mobile production. Distinct commissioned character models and distinct voices would improve the show's identity.

ECHO Studio — implementation research

Research date: 16 October 2026. Primary documentation, repositories, example pages and maintainer issue threads were retrieved. No external demo was visually executed during this research. “Example” below means published executable example/source, not an independently validated device benchmark. No complete browser seated podcast was verified; the defensible route is composing proven building blocks.

Eight relevant examples

Three strongest approaches

1. Existing Three.js rig + custom dialogue director — recommended conditionally

- What is evidenced: official examples support independent skinned clones, body animation and facial morph control. Three.js source and MIT license.

- Reuse: existing loader, avatar GLB, materials and speech assets after inspecting their provenance; one scene and renderer, a small set of camera transforms, procedural pose layers on the existing skeleton.

- Asset restrictions: Three.js MIT does not license ECHO's GLB. Preserve its existing credits and independently inspect provenance before publishing any newly introduced asset. No third-party asset is recommended solely because it can be downloaded.

- Maintenance/compatibility: stay on the project's installed Three.js version and use its matching addons. Current official documentation and runnable examples are available; no unverified commit-frequency claim is made.

- Supporting discussion: skinned-character performance investigation. A reporter ultimately isolated their slowdown to physics. This is a useful profiling lesson, not a transferable benchmark.

- Mobile feasibility / effort (engineering estimate): best fit and lowest integration cost if the rig already exposes leg/arm/head bones and face morphs. Three seated characters, bounded DPR, restrained materials and no postprocessing are a sensible initial budget; measure the finished scene. Procedural elbow/wrist placement still needs visual QA.

- Paid services: none required. Use local clips or clearly labeled device speech fallback.

2. TalkingHead avatarOnly inside the existing scene

- Reuse: face/speech controller, gaze targets and shared-scene armatures; seated animation still requires compatible bones and verified chair/table placement.

- License: MIT code. README distinguishes CC0 MPFB sample from noncommercial RPM/other samples. Do not assume all samples share the code license.

- Compatibility: Mixamo-compatible skeleton plus ARKit and Oculus face shapes. Default TTS integration uses Google Cloud; external audio is possible, so paid service is optional.

- Maintenance evidence: release notes document experimental multi-avatar support, disposal and audio interruption fixes. Issue 124 reports compressed avatar and morph-target compatibility problems; a warning to inspect actual inputs, not proof all avatars fail.

- Mobile / effort (inference): medium integration cost, potentially high if current morph targets differ. Three instances should share one renderer/loop. No verified three-avatar mobile benchmark.

3. three-vrm standardized avatar pipeline

- Repository/demo: three-vrm, linked examples above. Reuse humanoid pose access, facial expressions and look-at smoothing.

- License/restrictions: MIT runtime; each avatar's author license and VRM metadata remain separate. Require explicit redistribution permission for browser-delivered models.

- Maintenance evidence: release page lists v3.5.5 and v3.6.0-beta.0, with documented material and loader fixes. Pin a compatible stable version. README warns WebGPU node-material compatibility changes more often; retain WebGL for this prototype.

- Supporting discussion: duplicate animation-loop issue illustrates why playback actions must not create extra requestAnimationFrame chains. Issue list includes pose-retargeting concerns; validate imported clips.

- Mobile / effort (inference): viable with appropriately simple VRM assets, limited spring bones and material passes, but highest migration effort if ECHO is ordinary GLB. No measured phone performance asserted.

- Paid services: none required for runtime; asset creation/licensing remains a separate choice.

Why the first approach wins for this iteration

It protects the existing character lab and comparison modes, avoids a rig-format migration, and spends the effort on composition, contact, pacing and performance. Before committing: inspect bone names and rest transforms, morph names, triangle/material counts, model scale and license. If seated pose is impossible without obvious deformation, use a documented replacement or table-obscured lower-body framing and state that compromise. Do not describe rigid portraits as seated humanoids.

Theatre.js is optional authoring infrastructure, not a necessary dependency. Its core is Apache 2.0 while its editor is AGPL 3.0. A small event-driven director is easier to keep provider-neutral and to test for this scope.

Implementation implications (design proposals, not external claims)

1. One forest/sage/ivory room; curved table and three chairs in a shallow arc; fixed camera axis on the audience side. Pose hips/thighs/knees deliberately, place wrists above or beside the table, avoid imported standing gestures that pull elbows through furniture.

2. Author separate portrait/landscape shot transforms: establishing wide, host medium, both guest mediums, two-person view, selected listener reaction. Choose cuts only from sentence/turn cues, normally after 5–9 seconds; retain a shot through short interjections.

3. One transport clock drives captions, audio progress, face animation and director decisions. Provider adapter emits turn start/end, speaker/text, playback timing, optional visemes/emotion/gesture and cancellation/failure. A mock scripted adapter must be visibly identified.

4. Independent blink phase, small breathing and bounded head gaze. Sparse cue-driven nods. Mouth motion from amplitude or scheduled syllables must not be described as phoneme-accurate.

5. Begin with capped DPR, no screen-space effects and minimal shadow work. Pause the loop on hidden pages; dispose on navigation. Record renderer statistics and actual timing on tested devices, with device/context noted.

6. Explicit gesture starts playback. Pause/resume/replay/mute and cancellation share the same transport, not extra loops or Audio elements. Loading, missing audio, failed model and no-WebGL states must remain navigable with readable transcript.

Credits and evidence discipline

No new model was downloaded or installed for this research. The links above are research references, not a claim their assets ship in ECHO. Add actual shipped-asset credits only after source inspection. No scripts from forums were installed. Repository activity above reflects the retrieved pages; ambiguous yearless release timestamps are deliberately not interpreted. No measured FPS, seated-contact verification or audible synchronization verification is claimed by this document.
